topic: LLM Embeddings: How AI Understands Meaning
description: Check your understanding of embeddings, vectorization, semantic similarity, and how AI distinguishes words with multiple meanings.

questions.question: What is the key difference between token IDs and embeddings?
options: They are the same thing with different names
Token IDs are meaningless lookup numbers; embeddings are vectors that capture meaning
Token IDs are for English; embeddings are for other languages
questions.explanation: Token ID 8123 for 'Dog' is just a vocabulary lookup — no relationship to 8521 for 'Grapes'. Embeddings are dense numerical vectors where similar concepts (King–Queen) sit close together.

questions.question: How does an LLM know 'apple' (fruit) vs 'Apple' (company)?
options: It reads a dictionary definition for each word
Contextual embeddings update based on surrounding words during processing
It asks the user to clarify every ambiguous word
questions.explanation: Initial token embeddings may be similar, but Transformers process surrounding tokens through multiple layers. 'I ate apple at Apple Store' — context changes each 'apple'/'Apple' representation differently.

questions.question: What is vectorization in the context of LLMs?
options: Converting images to text descriptions
Turning words, sentences, or documents into arrays of numbers (vectors)
Splitting text into individual characters
questions.explanation: Vectorization converts any information (text, images, documents) into numerical vectors so computers can do math on them. Embedding models create these vectors with thousands of learned dimensions.

questions.question: What does cosine similarity measure?
options: The physical distance between two servers
How close two embedding vectors are in direction — indicating semantic similarity
The cost of running an embedding model
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity compares the angle between two vectors. Similar direction = similar meaning. Used in search, RAG, clustering, and recommendation systems.

questions.question: What is the difference between token embedding and text embedding?
options: Token embedding is for images; text embedding is for words
Token embedding is per-piece for model processing; text embedding summarizes whole sentences/documents
They are identical — just different terminology
questions.explanation: Token embedding = one vector per token for reading/generating. Text embedding = one vector for an entire sentence/document for search, classification, or retrieval tasks.

questions.question: What role do positional embeddings play?
options: They determine the API pricing tier
They tell the model the order/position of each token in the sentence
They translate text between languages
questions.explanation: Positional embeddings give tokens a sense of order. 'Dog bites Man' vs 'Man bites Dog' — same words, different positions, completely different meanings.

questions.question: Can two false statements have high embedding similarity?
options: No — embeddings only match true statements
Yes — embeddings capture relatedness, not truth
Only if they use the exact same words
questions.explanation: Embeddings measure semantic relatedness, not factual accuracy. Two false statements on the same topic can be very similar in embedding space. Always verify facts separately from similarity scores.
